item.title: Building Legal Agents When You Can't See the Data - Jacob Lauritzen, CTO of Legora
item.description:
播客：Latent Space
People were asking us about Mythos and everything, even though I think realistically a lot of legal work does not require Mythos-level intelligence. Paralegals, gone. Yeah. Junior lawyers, gone. I don't need them.
[laughs] Um, that's actually not what we're seeing. And we had one problem where, like, it wouldn't cite properly, and so we were like, "Next model release solved."
It went from, like, [laughs] seventy percent to, like, ninety-nine. It's just like we did nothing and, like, great. But if you're doing a, you know, four hundred million dollar M&A transaction, you're gonna want Lagora.
We're just gonna be twenty engineers for the rest of the company's history, and, like, we're gonna beat everyone who's much bigger. Uh, we're a hundred engineers now, and it feels like we're way too small.
But it's something that I'm toying with is, like, how much of our product can just be the agent versus all the other stuff?
[upbeat music] Okay, we're here in the studio with special guest, uh, Jacob Lauridsen, CTO of Lagora. Did I get it right, Lauridsen? Lauridsen. That's fine. Yeah, that's okay. And that's Danish.
I'm not super sure that how... It's Danish, yeah, exactly. Does it have a special history behind it? It's just, no, sen is like son, son of. Son of Laurits. So just like you have son and... Yeah.
[laughs] So son of Laurits, that's my name. [laughs] Nice. Uh, we've crossed paths here and there. You, you, you spoke at, uh, AI a few times, and obviously Lagora is one of the fastest-growing legal tech in history.
Yep. And, uh, y- you said something at the start in our pre-show that I thought was really interesting. You said that your origin is very European. Mm-hmm.
Uh, even though obviously you're expanding in New York and SF, what feels different about your culture? I think we are
just at the core probably very, uh, humble about what we're doing because we've always been the underdog from the very beginning.
No one believed the smallest startup in a basement in Stockholm was gonna, you know, out-compete this huge behemoth that was, like, way, yeah, ahead of us in the US.
So I think we've always been underdogs, and so we've always been very humble. Um, we've always sort of had to fight for our, uh, existence.
Um, I think something we've had to learn as we've also become more and more, um...
as we've entered the US and been in the US a lot more, is to be a little bit more, uh, bold and, like, s-s-tell the world how great we are 'cause it, it doesn't come naturally to, I think, some of us.
I kinda wanna start by going over your guys' product, 'cause I feel like with a lot of these, like, legal products, you know, they're kinda, like, under wraps. Like, you know- Yeah, sure. [laughs]...
you're not supposed to, like, show it. But, um, yeah, if you could just talk about, like, what does the product look like and maybe, like, how did you guys get there?
Like, like, what have been the product iterations that got you- Hmm... to where you are today? I think that would be really interesting. Yeah, absolutely.
The way everything started was ChatGPT with, uh, Swedish laws- Okay... and search tool in it. That was literally the entire everything. And so that's where we started.
We started with legal research, which is, like, a huge market basically in the world where, um, lawyers spend a lot of time figuring out what are previous cases that look like this? What's the legal precedent?
Like, is this... You know, what have previous people done in these situations? That's extremely important. Um, and so that has always been part of our product.
Basically, we started from, like, an, an agent you could ask questions, then it would query laws. That was the very simple beginning.
Um, and then from that, it's expanded, and so it's expanded in, like, what can the agent do? It, it will now, uh, you know, draft a lot of stuff really well. It will edit Word files.
It will, you know, move your files away, organize everything, um, run really complex analyses. Um, and we've added just a bunch more features to it.
So one of our features is called Tabular Review, which is, um, now a name that's being used in industry, [laughs] and we're very happy to see Claude for legal using our terminology- [laughs]... for what they're building.
[laughs] Ooh, we gotta talk about that. We gotta talk about that.
Which is essentially, like, a way to just bulk extract and bulk review many, many, many, um, agreements which you do in due diligence and when you raise money or whatever. So that's part of it.
It's like we help lawyers just do their work much more efficiently, much, much better.
And then outside of just doing the work, we're also now, um, helping orchestrate the work a lot more than we were just even a year ago.
So we have different sort of-- We have a, a thing called Lists, which is s-sort of like Linear for us. And, um, we have Intake, which is a way to collaborate with, um, clients.
And we have, um, Portal, which is also sort of a way to collaborate, you know, lawyer to lawyer, client to lawyer, lawyer to agent, agent to agent maybe.
[laughs] We're, we're spending a lot of time there 'cause, um, there's just frankly the way that you work with a lawyer ten years ago or maybe even today is, is really painful, and there's loads of room to do that- [laughs]...
in a much better way, to be honest. [laughs] And so those are, like, I think the two things. It's, it's doing the work, and it's also, like, orchestrating the work. When did you guys start doing or building the agent?
So I mean, we've al-- We basically had to switch from the assistant to the agent- Yeah... we call it, right? Um, I guess that the agent, I don't know, I wanna say a year ago probably. Yeah.
Um, something like- So this is a rough timeline for people who are understanding. YC twenty twenty-three. Yes. Uh, and now you were, you were a YC founder as well. YC twenty-four. YC twenty-four.
Yeah, I was in YC twenty-three. Yeah. Lagora was twenty-four. Okay. And then, uh, so, so there is-- this is, like, a little bit pre a- pre, like, agents really taking off. Exactly, yeah.
And then, like, using models obviously changed everything. Yes. I mean, you know, in one, in one sense today, uh, you know, we had a preview of the products. Uh, it does look... Well, preview.
We had a private, uh, thing. But we will put up a video on the, on the YouTube. Private screening, yeah. It's mostly like ChatGPT for lawyers. Yeah. Right? Like a very- Yeah...
like, very fair to say that, but then, like, uh, the sidebar has a lot of nice custom tools like the Tabular View, uh, like the in-intake, which I really liked, uh, and, uh, you know, a bunch of other- Yeah... things.
Exactly. Yeah, that's, that's exactly what it is. It's, it's CoWork or ChatGPT- Yeah... just like really, really good for legal work.
And, yeah, the, the, the workflow for, like, uh, ei- either, like, in-house corporate lawyers, like, people, like, looking for upcoming regulations- Yeah... all these things.
And we can talk about m-more of the, the products there. Yeah. What models are you guys using underneath? Like, can you talk about that? I mean, we're using a, a bunch of different ones- Yeah...
depending on tasks, right? That's, um- Okay. And then that's not available to the lawyer to see. You guys pick- For the agent-... yourselves. Yeah. Well, we've been back and forth on this. Yeah. [laughs] Yeah.
[laughs] To be-- Just like everyone else, I think.
In the agent, there's a model selector for the primary model, but there are certain tools that we use different models in, and there's, like, Tabular View and, like, we, we try...
I think we found it most effective to subdivide the problem and, and, and route on, like, as we subdivide the task. But we do right now have a, a picker In the agent Mm-hmm.
I'm not sure if that's gonna stay there always, to be honest. Ah. Um, so yeah. Yeah, I mean, so I bring a little bit of context to this ...
